intro: Down the Rabbit Hole AUST is a local gardener Canberra homeowners call when a garden needs a specific job done: a bed planted out, a tired garden made over, shrubs pruned back into shape or fresh mulch before summer. The business is owned and run by Michael Robinson, and it is fully insured and ABN registered.

This page is for one-off and project work. If you would rather have the garden looked after on a fixed fortnightly or monthly cycle, see [scheduled garden maintenance](/garden-maintenance) instead. If you are looking for a gardener Canberra wide for a particular job, here is what we take on, how a job is quoted and when in the year each job is best done.

paras: Most gardening jobs start with a clear brief: what you want the garden to look like when the job is finished. From there the work might be clearing and replanting a bed, pruning shrubs and roses back into shape, edging and mulching beds, or a seasonal tidy before spring or winter.

Each job is quoted on its own, so you pay for the work you ask for, and nothing starts until you have agreed to the quote. Green waste removal is available, so prunings, weeds and old plants do not end up piled by the fence.

paras: A garden bed makeover is the most common project request. Plants that have struggled are cleared, weeds are pulled, the soil is turned and improved, new plants go in and the bed is edged and mulched. The result is a bed that is easier to keep on top of, whether you look after it yourself afterwards or book follow-up work.

If you are hiring a gardener Canberra wide for a makeover, it helps to say what you like and what you want to avoid, such as thirsty plants, prickly shrubs or anything that needs constant pruning. Hardy, frost-tolerant plants suit most Canberra gardens.

sections.h2: When to book each job in Canberra
paras: Canberra gardens run on a sharp calendar, and a good gardener Canberra wide works to it. Roses and deciduous shrubs are pruned in winter while they are dormant. Frost-tender plants are cut back in spring, once the risk of frost has passed. Spring is the best time to plant out beds, so new plants can establish before the summer heat.

Late spring is the time to mulch, holding moisture in the soil and keeping roots cool through hot, dry summers with water restrictions in mind. Autumn suits a clean-up after leaf drop, and it is a good time to plant trees and shrubs while the soil is still warm.

faqs.q: What jobs can I book a gardener Canberra wide for?
faqs.a: One-off and project jobs such as planting, garden bed makeovers, pruning, mulching and seasonal tidy-ups. If you want ongoing visits on a fixed cycle, that is our garden maintenance service.

faqs.q: What is the difference between gardening services and garden maintenance?
faqs.a: Gardening services are one-off or project jobs booked when you need them. Garden maintenance is a recurring schedule, usually fortnightly or monthly, for homes, rentals and strata properties.

faqs.q: When is the best time to plant in Canberra?
faqs.a: Spring, once the frost risk has passed, suits most plants. Autumn also works for trees and shrubs while the soil is still warm. Avoid planting in the middle of summer unless you can water regularly.

faqs.q: Can you help an elderly parent who can no longer manage the garden?
faqs.a: Yes. A one-off job that takes care of the heavy work, like weeding, pruning and mulching, is a common request. Family members can arrange the job and the quote on their behalf.

faqs.q: Can you take the green waste away?
faqs.a: Yes, green waste removal is available. Prunings, weeds and old plants can be loaded and taken away at the end of the job, so nothing is left for your green bin. Ask for it in your quote.
